newsitem.title: USA: Pixar CFO sees cyclical revenues.
newsitem.headline: Pixar CFO sees cyclical revenues.

text.p: Pixar Animation Studios chief financial officer Lawrence Levy said Monday the company's revenues are likely to be "lumpy" in the next few years reflecting the company's two year production schedule.
Pixar, which released "Toy Story" in 1995, is not scheduled to release another film until late 1998. The company plans another film two years later.

Levy, speaking to the Hambrecht and Quist Technology Conference, said the two year cycle will produce some years of lower revenue as the company incurs production costs without the revenues to offset them.

Analysts predict Pixar will report revenues of 27.9 million in 1997 with earnings per share of $0.24 a share. However, in 1998, analysts expect revenues to fall to $6.7 million and earnings to fall to a loss of around $0.09 a share.
